header.name: Advanced Ethnographic and Qualitative Research Methods
header.description: This course introduces diverse ethnographic methods and epistemologies in sociology/anthropology: participant observation, visual sources, archival documents, oral narratives, visual as well as digital resources. It exposes students to data gathering techniques, designing a research proposal, conducting structured and unstructured interviews, while at the same time introducing key debates on the conditions of producing knowledge. The course will encourage students to think reflexively while designing their research proposals, by asking how the social position of the researcher is connected to data production. Through this, questions of objectivity, interpretation, and social construction in the production of ethnographic knowledge will be explored, by bringing questions of power and the politics of representation in the production of social ‘facts’. At the end of the course, students will be able to be able to design research projects and write grant applications, while being reflexive of the location through which research is produced.
prerequisites_mandatory: B.Tech-SSH201 Social Science Research Methods/Research Methods Course of HCD/Any other Research Methods Course
prerequisites_mandatory_resolved: B.Tech-SSH201 Social Science Research Methods/Research Methods Course of HCD/Any other Research Methods Course

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to define the principal research methods of social anthropology: participant observation, visual sources, archival, oral narratives, virtual ethnography.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to explain a range of ethnographic field methods: field-based, historical, visual, virtual, objects as well as digital and discuss, interpretive techniques, reflexivity of the writing process and the effects of power relations on the creation of knowledge.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to apply the learnings in their own research proposals and reflect on the ethical implications within research.

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Students are able to design research proposals and develop grant writing skills.

lecture_topics: Course overview: the production of anthropological knowledge
Historical sources: documentary and Oral Narratives
Visual Methods: Photography and Films in the production of anthropological knowledge
Ethnography of Entanglements: Studying relations between people, environments, artefacts and algorithms
Ethnography as writing: fieldnotes and writing up
